literal: guest being outside oneself eating non-dying medicine even if desirable nature it is not.
translation: Even if it is the medicine of immortality, eating it all by oneself while a guest waits outside is not to be desired.
modern: விருந்தினர் வீட்டின் வெளியே காத்திருக்க, சாவாமையைத் தரும் அமிழ்தமே ஆனாலும் அதனைத் தான் மட்டும் உண்பது விரும்பத்தக்கது அன்று.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the supreme importance of hospitality in classical Tamil culture. The phrase 'சாவா மருந்து' refers to a medicine that prevents death, often understood as the nectar of immortality. The poet declares that even if one possesses such a miraculous substance, consuming it alone while a guest remains unfed outside is entirely undesirable. The words 'தான் உண்டல்' (eating by oneself) contrast sharply with the communal and generous spirit expected of a householder.
